title: Search a 2D Matrix II
description:
Write an efficient algorithm that searches for an integer `target` in an `m x n` integer `matrix`. The matrix has the following properties:

- Integers in each row are sorted in ascending (non-decreasing) order from left to right.
- Integers in each column are sorted in ascending (non-decreasing) order from top to bottom.

Return `true` if `target` is present in `matrix`, and `false` otherwise.

Note that unlike a fully flattened sorted matrix, the first element of a row may be smaller than the last element of the previous row.
constraints: All integers in each row are sorted in non-decreasing order.
All integers in each column are sorted in non-decreasing order.
hints: Starting at the top-left or bottom-right corner does not help decide whether to move horizontally or vertically.
Start at the top-right corner (0, n - 1) instead: everything to the left is smaller or equal, and everything below is greater or equal.
If matrix[r][c] > target, eliminate column c (c -= 1); if matrix[r][c] < target, eliminate row r (r += 1). Each step eliminates a full row or column, finishing in O(m + n) time.

examples.explanation: 5 appears at matrix[1][1]; starting at top-right (0, 4) = 15, the search moves left to 11, 7, 4, then down to 5.
20 is not present in the matrix, so the staircase search exits the matrix bounds and returns false.
